packet.claim: recover_json_object treats JSON objects nested inside arrays as top-level candidates, so an array of objects yields the last object instead of NO_OBJECT.
packet.execution_evidence: kernel recovery on input [{"a":1}, {"b":2}] answered {"b":2} while expected NO_OBJECT.
packet.expected: NO_OBJECT for an input that is a JSON array containing objects, because no top-level object exists.
packet.observed: k_recovery returns the canonical JSON of the last object in the array, e.g. {"b":2}.
packet.scope: Any reply whose text is a JSON array containing one or more objects (or any non-object container with object elements).
packet.source_basis: Every top-level balanced object in the text is a candidate... an object nested inside another is not a candidate of its own.
